learn.title: Tidal Stream Energy: Harnessing Ocean Currents
learn.intro: Unlike wind or solar, tides are driven by lunar gravity, making them incredibly predictable. As we transition to a carbon-free grid, tidal stream energy offers a reliable, high-density source of power that can be forecasted years in advance, providing a stable baseline for ocean-based renewable energy systems.
learn.c1_text: Think of tides like a scheduled train service. Because we know exactly when the moon's gravity pulls the ocean, we can predict energy output with near-perfect accuracy. This predictability helps grid operators balance supply and demand much more effectively than variable sources like wind.
learn.c2_text: Underwater turbines capture the kinetic energy of moving water. Because water is roughly 800 times denser than air, even slow-moving currents can generate massive amounts of power compared to wind turbines of the same size, making it a highly efficient energy source.
learn.c3_text: While still emerging, ocean energy represents a massive untapped resource. Integrating tidal streams into coastal grids can reduce reliance on fossil fuels in maritime regions, supporting global decarbonization goals through advanced subsea engineering and specialized turbine designs.
learn.stat1: Water density is ~800x higher than air

learn.title: Agrivoltaics: Solar Power Meets Farming
learn.intro: Land use competition is a major challenge for renewable expansion. Agrivoltaics solves this by co-locating solar panels and agriculture on the same plot. This dual-use approach maximizes land efficiency, improves water retention, and creates a symbiotic relationship between technology and nature.
learn.c1_text: Imagine a garden with built-in shades. Solar panels act as a protective canopy for crops, shielding them from harsh direct sunlight and reducing evaporation. This allows farmers to grow food and generate electricity simultaneously on the exact same acre of land.
learn.c2_text: The shade from panels lowers the temperature of the soil and the air around the plants. This creates a cooler microclimate, which reduces plant stress and significantly lowers the amount of water needed for irrigation through decreased evaporation rates.
learn.c3_text: In many regions, combining these technologies increases total land productivity. While solar provides income through energy, the crops benefit from reduced heat stress, creating a more resilient agricultural system against the increasing threats of climate-driven droughts and heatwaves.

learn.title: Floating Offshore Wind Platforms
learn.intro: Fixed-bottom offshore wind is limited to shallow waters. Floating platforms unlock the vast majority of offshore wind potential by allowing turbines to be placed in much deeper waters where winds are stronger and more consistent, revolutionizing how we harness marine wind energy.
learn.c1_text: Think of a buoy in the ocean. Instead of being bolted to the seabed, these turbines sit on floating structures moored to the floor. This allows us to move away from the coastline and into much deeper, windier ocean regions.
learn.c2_text: These platforms use advanced buoyancy and mooring systems to stay upright despite heavy waves. By using floating foundations, developers can access high-velocity wind corridors that were previously unreachable due to the extreme depths of the ocean floor.
learn.c3_text: Floating technology is essential for countries with narrow continental shelves. By moving further offshore, we can reduce visual impacts on coastlines and tap into much higher capacity factors, making offshore wind a cornerstone of the global energy transition.

learn.title: Flow Batteries for Grid-Scale Storage
learn.intro: As we add more intermittent renewables like wind and solar, we need long-duration storage. Flow batteries offer a scalable, durable alternative to lithium-ion, making it possible to store large amounts of energy for hours or even days to stabilize the grid.
learn.c1_text: Think of a large tank of fuel. Unlike standard batteries that store energy in solid electrodes, flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes kept in external tanks. This makes it very easy to scale up the capacity just by using larger tanks.
learn.c2_text: Vanadium redox flow batteries use different oxidation states of vanadium to store energy. These systems are incredibly durable, often lasting over 20 years with minimal degradation, making them ideal for massive, long-duration grid-scale applications.
learn.c3_text: By providing long-duration discharge, these batteries help smooth out the fluctuations of renewable energy. They act as a massive buffer, ensuring that even when the sun goes down or the wind stops, the grid remains stable and reliable.

learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar empowers consumers to become 'prosumers'—both producers and consumers of electricity. In India, government policies like net metering are crucial to incentivizing residential solar adoption, helping meet the nation's massive renewable energy targets.
learn.c1_text: Imagine your house has its own mini power plant. When your solar panels produce more electricity than you use during the day, that extra energy flows back into the local grid, turning your home into a tiny power station.
learn.c2_text: Net metering is a billing mechanism. The utility company tracks how much energy you take from the grid versus how much you give back. At the end of the month, you only pay for the 'net' amount you actually consumed.
learn.c3_text: The MNRE in India promotes rooftop solar to reduce peak load on the grid. Through various subsidies and net metering policies, India aims to rapidly increase decentralized solar capacity to support its growing energy demands and climate goals.

learn.title: Green Steel: Hydrogen-Based Production
learn.intro: Steel production is one of the hardest sectors to decarbonize. Traditionally reliant on coal, the shift toward 'Green Steel' using hydrogen as a reducing agent is a critical step in eliminating CO2 emissions from heavy industrial processes.
learn.c1_text: Think of hydrogen as a cleaner fuel. In a traditional blast furnace, coal is used to strip oxygen from iron ore. In green steel production, hydrogen is used instead, producing only pure water vapor as a byproduct.
learn.c2_text: The process involves Direct Reduced Iron technology. By using hydrogen gas in a reactor, the iron ore is chemically transformed into high-quality metallic iron without the massive carbon footprint associated with traditional coke-based smelting processes.
learn.c3_text: As global demand for low-carbon materials grows, green steel will become essential. This technology shift requires massive scaling of renewable energy to produce the green hydrogen needed to power these new, cleaner industrial-scale furnaces.
